For, apart from the accents, it would be quite at variance with the general use of the personal pronoun המה, to apply it to any other persons than those just described (viz., in any such sense as this: “And those, who ought to be shepherds, do not know”). Nor is it admissible to commence an adversative minor clause with והמה, as Knobel does, “whereas they are shepherds;” for, since the principal clause has  הכלבים (dogs) as the subject, this would introduce a heterogeneous mixture of the two figures, shepherds’ dogs and shepherds. We therefore take רעים והמה as an independent clause: “And it is upon men of such a kind, that the duty of watching and tending the nation devolves!” These רעים (for which the Targum reads רעים) are then still further described: they know not to understand, i.e., they are without spiritual capacity to pass an intelligible judgment (compare the opposite combination of the two verbs in <reference osisRef="Isa.32.4">Isa 32:4</reference>); instead of caring for the general good, they have all turned to their own way (<hi type="italic">ledarkâm</hi>), i.e., to their own selfish interests, every one bent upon his own advantage (בּצע from בּצע, <hi type="italic">abscindere</hi>, as we say, <hi type="italic">seinen Schnitt zu machen</hi>, to reap an advantage, lit., to make an incision). מקּצהוּ, from his utmost extremity (i.e., from that of his own station, including all its members), in other words, “throughout the length and breadth of his own circle;” <hi type="italic">qâtseh</hi>, the end, being regarded not as the terminal point, but as the circumference (as in <reference osisRef="Gen.19.4">Gen 19:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.47.21">Gen 47:21</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Jer.51.31">Jer 51:31</reference>).
entries.058c01ae53f438e3f00142cf02afd28ed1d1da1c: <reference osisRef="Isa.56.12">Isa 56:12</reference> <div eID="gen13558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13559" type="x-p"/> An office-bearer of the kind described is now introduced per mimesin as speaking. <hi type="italic">“Come here, I will fetch wine, and let us drink meth; and tomorrow shall be like today, great, excessively abundant.”</hi> He gives a banquet, and promises the guests that the revelry shall be as great tomorrow as today, or rather much more glorious. מחר יום is the day of tomorrow, τὸ ἐπαύριον, for <hi type="italic">mâchâr</hi> is always without an article; hence <hi type="italic">et fiet uti hic </hi>(<hi type="italic">dies</hi>)<hi type="italic">dies crastinus</hi>, viz., <hi type="italic">magnus supra modum valde</hi>. יתר, or יתר (as it is to be pointed here according to Kimchi, <hi type="italic">Michlol</hi> 167 <hi type="italic">b</hi>, and <hi type="italic">Wörterbuch</hi>), signifies superabundance; it is used here adverbially in the sense of extra-ordinarily, beyond all bounds (differing therefore from יותר, “more,” or “singularly,” in the book of Ecclesiastes).  <chapter eID="Isa.56"/> <div eID="gen13559" type="x-p"/>

                  <ns0:head>CHAP. LVI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 THus saith the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This verse and the rest of this Chapter, until <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9. seems to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />long to the foregoing Prophesie. From the consideration of Gods Promises made to them he moveth them to perform their duty to him.</ns0:note>, Keep ye <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> equity.</ns0:note> judgment, and do justice <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">This Phrase elsewhere signifies the duties which one man oweth to another, but here it seems to signifie the Duties which men owe to God, as it is explained in the following verses.</ns0:note>: for my salvation <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">That eminent Salvation by the Messiah so largely promised, and insisted upon in the foregoing Chapters: for which it behoves you to prepare your selves, and in which, without this condition you shall have no share nor benefit.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> near to come <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">So the Scripture useth to speak of things which are at a great distance, as if they were present or at hand. See <ns0:hi>Habak.</ns0:hi> 2. 3. <ns0:hi>Iam.</ns0:hi> 5. 8, 9. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 22. 20.</ns0:note>, and my righteousness <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The same thing which he now called <ns0:hi>Salvation,</ns0:hi> and here calleth his <ns0:hi>Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness,</ns0:hi> because it is an evident demonstration of Gods Righteous<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness as in the fulfilling of his promises, so in the punishment of sin, and in the salvation of sinners upon just and honourable terms.</ns0:note> to be revealed.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 Blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the man <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Every man, not only Jews, but Gentiles, or Strangers, as it is explained in the following Verses.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> doth this <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Judgment and Justice, men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1.</ns0:note>, and the son of man <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> layeth hold on it: that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That guardeth the Sabbath from profanation, that doth not defile it, ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther by forbidden practices, or by the neglect of commanded du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties. And though Sabbath seems to be put here, as Sacrifice is elsewhere, Synecdochically for the whole Worship of God, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of this is an eminent part, and the bond of all the rest.</ns0:note>, and keepeth his hand <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which being the great instrument of Action, is put for all the kinds and means of Action.</ns0:note> from doing any evil <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">To wit, to ones Neighbour, as it is more fully expressed, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 15. 3.</ns0:note>. <ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>h</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>that holdeth it fast,</ns0:hi> that is resolute and constant in so doing, that not only begins well, but perseveres in it.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 Neither let the son of a stranger <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The stranger, as <ns0:hi>the son of man</ns0:hi> is the same with <ns0:hi>the man, v.</ns0:hi> 2. the Gentile, who by Birth is a stranger to God, and to the Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon-Wealth of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, that hath joined himself to the LORD <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That hath turned from dumb Idols to the living God, and to the true Religion: for such shall be as ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptable to me as the Israelites themselves, and the partition-wall between Jews and Gentiles shall be taken down, and Repentance and Remission of sins shall be preached and offered to men of all Nations.</ns0:note> speak, saying, The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people, neither let the eunuch <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Who is here joined with the stranger, because he was forbidden to <ns0:hi>enter into the Congregation of the Lord,</ns0:hi> Deut. 23. 1. as the stranger was, and by his barrenness might seem no less than the stranger to be cast out of Gods Covenant, and cut off from his People, to whom the blessing of a numerous Posterity was promised. And under these two Instances he understands all those persons, who either by Birth, or by any Ceremonial Pollution, were excluded from the participation of Church priviledges, and so he throws open the door to all true Believers without any re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />striction whatsoever.</ns0:note> say, Behold, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> a dry tree <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">A sapless and fruitless Tree, accursed by God with the curse of barrenness, which being oft threatned as a Curse, and being a matter of Reproach among the Jews might ea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sily occasion such discouraging thoughts as are here expressed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 For thus saith the LORD unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose <ns0:hi>the things</ns0:hi> that please me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That observe my commands not by custom, or force, or fear, but by free choice, and full consent, with love to them and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />light in them.</ns0:note>, and take hold of my covenant <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">That resolvedly and steadfastly keep the condi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions of my Covenant.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Even unto them will I give in mine house <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">In my Temple, to serve me there as Priests, which Eunuchs were not allowed to do, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 21. 17, &c. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 23. 1.</ns0:note>, and within my walls <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">In the Courts of my Temple, which were encompassed with Walls. This seems to be added with respect to the People who were admitted into the Court, but not into the House it self.</ns0:note>, a place and a name better than of sons and daughters <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">A far greater Blessing and Honour than that of having posterity, which was but a temporal Mercy, and that common to the worst of men, even my Favour, and my Spirit, and eternal Felicity.</ns0:note>: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">That with purpose of heart cleave unto him, as is said, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 11. 23..</ns0:note>, to serve him, and to love the name of the LORD <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">To serve him out of love to him, and to his Worship.</ns0:note>, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 Even them will I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 2. 2.</ns0:note> bring to my holy mountain <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">To my house, as it is explained in the following clause, which stood upon Mount <ns0:hi>Sion,</ns0:hi> largely so called, including Mount <ns0:hi>Moriah.</ns0:hi> Formerly the Gentiles neither had any de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sire to come thither, nor were admitted there; but now I will incline their hearts to come, and I will give them ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mission and free liberty to come into my Church.</ns0:note>, and make them joyful <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">By accept<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing their services, and comforting their hearts with the sense of my Love, and pouring down all sorts of blessings upon them.</ns0:note> in my house of prayer <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">In my Temple, in and towards which Prayers are daily made and direct<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed unto me, 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 8. 19, 28.</ns0:note>: their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on mine altar <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">They shall have as free access to mine House and Altar, as the Jews themselves, and their ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vices shall be as acceptable to me as theirs. Evangelical Worship is here described under such Expressions as agreed to the Worship of God which then was in use, as it is <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 1. 11. and elsewhere. See also <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12. 1. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13. 15.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 21. 13. Mar. 11. 17. Luk. 19. 46.</ns0:note> mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Jews and Gentiles shall have equal freedom of access to my House, and shall there call upon my Name. Possibly he may call it <ns0:hi>an House of Prayer,</ns0:hi> either to imply that Prayer to God, whereof Thanksgiving is a part, is a more considerable part of Gods Worship than Sacrifice, which being considered in itself is little valued by him, as he frequently decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reth: or to signifie that in the New Testament, when the Gentiles should be called, all other Sacrifices should cease, except that of Prayer, and such like Spiritual Services. Which also is confirmed from the nature of the thing. For seeing Sacrifices were confined to the Temple at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and it was impossible that all Nations should resort thither to offer up Levitical Sacrifices in such time and manner as God appointed, it was necessary upon supposition of the general conversion of the Gentiles, that that way of Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship ship should be abolished, and such a way prescribed as they were capable of practising.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:617" />8 The Lord GOD, which gathereth the out-casts of Israel <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Which will gather to himself, and bring into their own Land, those poor Israelites which are, or shall be, cast out of their own Land, and from Gods presence, and dispersed in divers parts of the World.</ns0:note>, saith, Yet will I gather <ns0:hi>others</ns0:hi> to him, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> to his gathered.</ns0:note> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides those that are gathered unto him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">As there are some few Gentiles whom I have made Proselytes, and added to the Jewish Church, so I shall make ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther and a far more comprehensive gathering of the Gentiles, whom I shall bring into the same Church with the Jews, making both Jews and Gentiles one fold under one Shepherd, as it is pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 10. 16.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, <ns0:hi>yea,</ns0:hi> all ye beasts in the forrest <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This invitation or proclamation is a prediction of <ns0:hi>Israel's</ns0:hi> De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction by their cruel Enemies, which are oft expressed in Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture under the names of ravenous Beasts. But the great Question is, What connexion this part of the Chapter hath with the for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer? Which may be thus conceived: The prophet having largely dis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>sed concerning the Messiah, and his Church and Kingdom, and particularly of the great accession and conversion of the Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles to it, and of the Infidelity, Apostacy, and manifold Wicked<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses of the Jewish Nation, and having comforted and encouraged the Gentiles with Gods gracious promises made to them, he now proceeds to terrifie the unbelieving and ungodly Jews, and to shew that as the Gentiles should believe, and be saved, so they should reject their Messiah, and be utterly destroyed; although we need not labour much about the coherence: For this may be a new Sermon, and therefore many learned Interpreters make this the beginning of the 57th Chapter.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 His <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Israels,</ns0:hi> as is evident from the following verses: the Pronoun Relative being put without, and instead of the Antecedent; of which I have given divers Instances before.</ns0:note> watchmen <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Priests and Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, or other Teachers, who are commonly called <ns0:hi>Watchmen,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 3. 17. & 33. 2. <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 9. 8. He mentions only the Teachers, because Ignorance was most shameful in them, but hereby he sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poseth the gross ignorance of the People, who neither pretended nor desired to be wiser than their Teachers.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> blind: they are all igno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rant <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Of Gods Will and Word, and of their own and the Peoples duty, and of the true Messiah.</ns0:note>, they <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> all dumb dogs, they cannot bark <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">They are also slothful and negligent in instructing the people, and do not faithfully reprove them for their sins, nor warn them of their dangers, nor keep them from Errours and cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ruptions in Doctrine, and Worship, and Conversation, as they ought to do.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>dreaming,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>talking in their sleep.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Minding their own ease and safety more than the Peoples benefit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 Yea, they <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi>

                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> strong of appetite.</ns0:note> greedy dogs <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> know not to be satis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fied.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 34. 2, 3.</ns0:note> can ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver have enough <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Insatiably covetous.</ns0:note>, and they <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> shepherds that cannot understand <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>that know not to understand,</ns0:hi> that do not care, or love, or desire (as <ns0:hi>knowing</ns0:hi> is frequently taken) ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther to understand the Law, or Word of God themselves, or to make the People to understand it.</ns0:note>: they <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 53. 6. & 57. 17.</ns0:note> all look to their own way <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">They regard neither Gods Command and Glory, nor the Peoples good, but only the satisfacti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of their own base Lusts. See on <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53. 6.</ns0:note>, eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry one for his gain from his quarter <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">In their several places and stations, as they have opportunity: Heb. <ns0:hi>from his</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>their end</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>extremity, i. e.</ns0:hi> universally, or all from one end of that Body or Society of men unto the other: as the same word signifies <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 19. 4. from one end of the City to the other, or, as we there render it, <ns0:hi>from every quarter:</ns0:hi> and as the same word is by divers learned Men rendred 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 12. 31. not <ns0:hi>of the meanest</ns0:hi> of the people, but <ns0:hi>out of all</ns0:hi> the people, or indifferently out of every Tribe: of which see my note there.                   <ns0:p n="12">12 Come ye, <ns0:hi>say they</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Unto their Brethren, by Office, and in Iniquity, unto their Fellow-Priests, or other jolly companions.</ns0:note>, I will fetch wine, and we will fill our selves <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">We will drink not only to Delight, but even to Drunkenness, as this word signifies, <ns0:hi>Mich.</ns0:hi> 1. 10. and elsewhere.</ns0:note> with strong drink, and to morrow shall be as this day, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> much more abundant <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Which sheweth their dreadful se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />curity and contempt of God, and of his Judgments, and their to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tal and resolved abandoning of all care of their own or Peoples Souls.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
